title: SIU clears cops in Hwy. 417 shooting
article: The province's Special Investigations Unit has cleared an Ottawa cop in the April shooting death of a 43-year-old Montreal man partly because the man died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound to the head.
The SIU investigation determined Richard Bastien got out of his car carrying a revolver and three officers "interacted" with him at 5:30 p.m. April 22.
During this interaction, a number of shots were fired and Bastien was hit.
He died two days later at the Ottawa Hospital's Civic campus.
The SIU says Bastien pointed his revolver at police and an officer began shooting at Bastien from inside his cruiser.

"One of the rounds struck Bastien. Almost simultaneously, Bastien shot himself in the left temple area of his head. According to the autopsy, the self-inflicted wound, and not the wound inflicted by the officer, was the fatal one," SIU director Ian Scott said in a news release.
Police began pursuing Bastien after a shooting in the Carp area.
The vehicle stopped at Hwy. 417 and Walkley Rd., where the confrontation with police occurred.
Scott said the officer had reasonable grounds to believe Bastien posed a threat.
